correctness.rationale: With center line L, Psi(L,T)=B_q(r)−B_q(dim(T∩L)). The entry time for rank-r subspaces containing L is B_q(r)−2 and for those avoiding L is B_q(r)−1. At birth b_k=B_q(k)−1, the whole rank≤k proper-bottom subspace lattice is present and its EL-shellability concentrates reduced integral homology in degree k−1. The truncated Gaussian-Möbius partial sum gives q^{k(k+1)/2}{n−1 choose k}_q classes. At d_k=B_q(k+1)−2, T↦T+L is a well-defined extensive monotone idempotent closure of precisely that filtration stage to a conical image with minimum L; all classes die. No changes between birth and death or prior to the next birth, so integer modules split into the stated finite bars and one essential H0 bar. Independently verified 105 Gaussian partial-sum identities for q=2,3,4,5,8 and n≤7; the published source verifier was read, not blindly trusted. Exact all-prime-power proof uses geometric-lattice shellability and closure operators, not finite arithmetic.
residual_risks: The shellability and homology facts are standard and reused; originality concerns the center-dependent integral barcode and death maps, not rank Betti numbers.

originality.rationale: The same finite-space furtherness function and degree-zero theory are already present in Badra–Singh 2026, and rank-selected geometric-lattice sphere wedges are classical; those ingredients are credited. The final claim instead identifies an integral barcode in every degree for a line-centered non-distributive projective subspace lattice with explicit Gaussian multiplicities and closure-controlled deaths. Kitajima 2026 is a plausible general rank-filtered competitor: its accessible abstract covers rank-defined filtrations and homotopy types, not the two-stage line-centered weights, but its full text was unavailable (arXiv/OA failed; institutional VPN disconnected). On present evidence, that access limitation is a specific priority risk, not a scientific failure.
